pages.caption: Once upon a time there was a princess who was the prettiest creature in the world.
pages.scene: Princess Goldilocks walks through her garden

pages.caption: And because she was so beautiful, and because her hair was like the finest gold, and waved and rippled nearly to the ground, she was called Pretty Goldilocks.
pages.description: [Goldilocks with golden hair and flower crown]
pages.scene: Goldilocks with golden hair and flower crown

pages.caption: She always wore a crown of flowers, and her dresses were embroidered with diamonds and pearls, and everybody who saw her fell in love with her.
pages.scene: She wears a crown of flowers

pages.caption: Now one of her neighbors was a young king who was not married.
pages.description: [Young king looks longingly toward her kingdom]
pages.scene: Young king looks longingly toward her kingdom

pages.caption: He was very rich and handsome, and when he heard all that was said about Pretty Goldilocks, though he had never seen her, he fell so deeply in love with her that he could neither eat nor drink.
pages.scene: King gazes at portrait of Goldilocks

pages.caption: So he resolved to send an ambassador to ask her in marriage.
pages.scene: Kings messenger sets out with horses

pages.caption: He had a splendid carriage made for his ambassador, and gave him more than a hundred horses and a hundred servants, and told him to be sure and bring the Princess back with him.
pages.scene: Ambassador arrives at palace gate

pages.caption: After he had started nothing else was talked of at Court, and the King felt so sure that the Princess would consent that he set his people to work at pretty dresses and splendid furniture.
pages.scene: Goldilocks declines the proposal

pages.caption: When the ambassador reached the city, where the King was waiting impatiently, everybody was very much annoyed with him for not bringing the Princess.
pages.scene: Ambassador returns sadly alone

pages.caption: And the King cried like a baby, and nobody could console him.
pages.scene: King weeps on his throne

pages.caption: Now there was at the Court a young man, who was more clever and handsome than anyone else.
pages.scene: Charming speaks to the court

pages.caption: If the King had sent me to the Princess Goldilocks I am sure she would have come back with me.
pages.scene: Charming proudly makes his claim

pages.caption: Ha, ha! said he; does he laugh at my unhappiness, and think himself more fascinating than I am? Go, and let him be shut up in my great tower to die of hunger.
pages.scene: King orders Charming imprisoned

pages.caption: So the King's guards went to fetch Charming, who had thought no more of his rash speech, and carried him off to prison with great cruelty.
pages.scene: Guards drag Charming to the tower

pages.caption: The poor prisoner had only a little straw for his bed, and but for a little stream of water which flowed through the tower he would have died of thirst.
pages.scene: Charming alone in the dark tower

pages.caption: One day when he was in despair he said to himself: How can I have offended the King?
pages.scene: King passes by the tower

pages.caption: The King chanced to be passing the tower and recognized the voice of his former favorite.
pages.scene: King listens outside the tower

pages.caption: And then he opened the tower door and called to Charming, who came very sadly and kissed the King's hand.
pages.scene: Charming kneels before the king

pages.caption: So he took Charming back to the palace with him, and after seeing that he had a very good supper he said to him.
pages.scene: King restores Charming to favor

pages.caption: Charming replied that he was perfectly willing to go, and would set out the very next day.
pages.scene: Charming sets out on his quest

pages.caption: It was on a Monday morning that he set out all alone upon his errand.
pages.scene: Charming rides through a meadow

pages.caption: When he had written it down he was looking round him, pleased to find himself in such a pretty place, when all at once he saw a great golden carp lying gasping and exhausted upon the grass.
pages.description: [Charming finds the carp on the grass]
pages.scene: Charming finds the carp on the grass

pages.caption: Charming had pity upon her, and, though he could not help thinking that she would have been very nice for dinner, he picked her up gently and put her back into the water.
pages.scene: Charming gently returns carp to water

pages.caption: I thank you, Charming, for the kindness you have done me. You have saved my life; one day I will repay you.
pages.scene: Dame Carp speaks from the water

pages.caption: Another day, as he journeyed on, he saw a raven in great distress. The poor bird was closely pursued by an eagle, which would soon have eaten it up, had not Charming quickly fitted an arrow to his bow and shot the eagle dead.
pages.description: [Charming shoots the eagle attacking a raven]
pages.scene: Charming shoots the eagle attacking a raven

pages.caption: Charming, said he, it was very generous of you to rescue a poor raven; I am not ungrateful, some day I will repay you.
pages.description: [The raven thanks Charming from the tree]
pages.scene: The raven thanks Charming from the tree

pages.caption: Before the sun rose he found himself in a thick wood where it was too dark for him to see his path, and here he heard an owl crying as if it were in despair.
pages.description: [Charming cuts the owl free from the net]
pages.scene: Charming cuts the owl free from the net

pages.caption: It does not need many words to tell you how great a service you have done me. I was caught; in a few minutes the fowlers would have been here.
pages.scene: Owl speaks to Charming

pages.caption: These three adventures were the only ones of any consequence that befell Charming upon his journey, and he made all the haste he could to reach the palace of the Princess Goldilocks.
pages.description: [Charming arrives at the palace of Goldilocks]
pages.scene: Charming arrives at the palace of Goldilocks

pages.caption: When he arrived he thought everything he saw delightful and magnificent.
pages.scene: Goldilocks prepares on her throne

pages.caption: Then he dressed himself carefully in rich brocade, with scarlet and white plumes, and threw a splendid embroidered scarf over his shoulder.
pages.scene: Goldilocks descends the staircase

pages.caption: Then Charming was led in, and was so struck with astonishment and admiration that at first not a word could he say.
pages.scene: Charming presents his harangue

pages.caption: Sir Charming, answered she, all the reasons you have given me are very good ones, and I assure you that I should have more pleasure in obliging you than anyone else.
pages.description: [Goldilocks tells him of the lost ring]
pages.scene: Goldilocks tells him of the lost ring

pages.caption: As I valued it more than my kingdom, you may imagine how vexed I was at losing it, and I vowed to never listen to any proposal of marriage unless the ambassador first brought me back my ring.
pages.scene: Goldilocks points to the river

pages.caption: When he got back to his lodging he went to bed without eating any supper, and his little dog, who was called Frisk, could not eat any either.
pages.scene: Charming mourns by his bed

pages.caption: My dear master, do not despair; the luck may change, you are too good not to be happy.
pages.scene: Frisk comforts Charming

pages.caption: At the first glimmer of dawn Frisk began to jump about, and when he had waked Charming they went out together, first into the garden, and then down to the river's brink.
pages.scene: Frisk leads Charming to the river

pages.caption: You saved my life in the meadow by the willow tree, and I promised that I would repay you. Take this, it is Princess Goldilock's ring.
pages.scene: Dame Carp surfaces with the ring

pages.caption: So in came Charming, who presented her with the ring and said: Madam, I have done your bidding. Will it please you to marry the King my master?
pages.scene: Charming returns the ring to Goldilocks

pages.caption: When the Princess saw her ring brought back to her unhurt she was so astonished that she thought she must be dreaming.
pages.scene: Goldilocks gazes at her restored ring

pages.caption: There is a prince not far from here whose name is Galifron, who once wanted to marry me, but when I refused he uttered the most terrible threats against me.
pages.scene: Goldilocks tells Charming of the giant

pages.caption: Very well, Princess, I will fight this Galifron; I believe that he will kill me, but at any rate I shall die in your defense.
pages.scene: Charming rides toward the giant's castle

pages.caption: At last he drew near the giant's castle, and saw to his horror that every path that led to it was strewn with bones.
pages.description: [Bones line the path to the castle]
pages.scene: Bones line the path to the castle

pages.caption: Before long he saw Galifron coming. His head was higher than the tallest trees, and he sang in a terrible voice.
pages.scene: Giant Galifron towers over the trees

pages.caption: When Galifron heard these words he looked all about him, and saw Charming standing, sword in hand.
pages.description: [The raven pecks at the giant's eyes]
pages.scene: The raven pecks at the giant's eyes

pages.caption: The raven, pecking with its strong beak and beating with its great wings so confused and blinded him that all his blows fell harmlessly upon the air.
pages.scene: Charming defeats the giant

pages.caption: And then he mounted his horse and rode off with Galifron's head.
pages.scene: Charming cuts off the giant's head

pages.caption: Princess, said Charming, I have killed your enemy; I hope you will now consent to marry the King my master.
pages.scene: Charming presents the head to Goldilocks

pages.caption: Oh dear! no, said the Princess, not until you have brought me some water from the Gloomy Cavern.
pages.scene: Goldilocks describes the Gloomy Cavern

pages.caption: Not far from here there is a deep cave, the entrance to which is guarded by two dragons with fiery eyes, who will not allow anyone to pass them.
pages.scene: Dragons guard the cavern entrance

pages.caption: Charming, quite determined to get the water or die, now drew his sword.
pages.description: [Charming draws his sword before the dragon]
pages.scene: Charming draws his sword before the dragon

pages.caption: You saved my life when I was caught in the net, now I can repay you. Trust me with the flask, for I know all the ways of the Gloomy Cavern.
pages.scene: Owl offers to fill the flask

pages.caption: Charming was only too glad to give her the flask, and she flitted into the cavern quite unnoticed by the dragon.
pages.description: [Owl flies into the cavern with the flask]
pages.scene: Owl flies into the cavern with the flask

pages.caption: And after some time returned with the flask, filled to the very brim with sparkling water.
pages.scene: Owl returns with the filled flask

pages.caption: He went straight to the palace and gave the flask to the Princess, who had no further objection to make.
pages.scene: Charming and Goldilocks journey together

pages.caption: The Princess found Charming such an agreeable companion that she sometimes said to him: Why did not we stay where we were?
pages.description: [Goldilocks and Charming ride through the countryside]
pages.scene: Goldilocks and Charming ride through the countryside

pages.caption: At last they reached the King's great city, and he came out to meet the Princess, bringing magnificent presents.
pages.description: [King greets them at the city gates]
pages.scene: King greets them at the city gates

pages.caption: And the marriage was celebrated with great rejoicings.
pages.scene: The wedding celebration

pages.caption: If it had not been for Charming, she said to the King, I should never have come here.
pages.scene: Charming speaks to the King

pages.caption: Then Charming's enemies said to the King: It is a wonder that you are not jealous, the Queen thinks there is nobody in the world like Charming.
pages.scene: Enemies whisper to the King

pages.caption: It is quite true, now I come to think of it, said the King. Let him be chained hand and foot, and thrown into the tower.
pages.scene: King orders Charming chained again

pages.caption: So they took Charming, and as a reward for having served the King so faithfully he was shut up in the tower.
pages.description: [Charming imprisoned in the tower once more]
pages.scene: Charming imprisoned in the tower once more

pages.caption: However, little Frisk came to console him, and told him all the news.
pages.scene: Frisk consoles Charming in prison

pages.caption: When Pretty Goldilocks heard what had happened she threw herself at the King's feet and begged him to set Charming free.
pages.description: [Goldilocks begs the King to free Charming]
pages.scene: Goldilocks begs the King to free Charming

pages.caption: So, when the King, thinking to improve his beauty, took the flask and sprinkled the water upon his face, he fell asleep, and nobody could wake him.
pages.scene: King accidentally uses the sleep water

pages.caption: Little Frisk was the first to hear the news, and he ran to tell Charming.
pages.description: [Frisk runs to Charming with the news]
pages.scene: Frisk runs to Charming with the news

pages.caption: Then she remembered all he had done for her, and without saying a word to anyone went straight to the tower, and with her own hands took off Charming's chains.
pages.scene: Goldilocks frees Charming from his chains

pages.caption: Come, faithful Charming, I make you king, and will take you for my husband.
pages.scene: Goldilocks crowns Charming as king

pages.caption: Everybody was delighted that he should be king, and the wedding, which took place at once, was the prettiest that can be imagined.
pages.scene: The final wedding celebration

pages.caption: And Prince Charming and Princess Goldilocks lived happily ever after.
pages.description: [Charming and Goldilocks live happily ever after]
pages.scene: Charming and Goldilocks live happily ever after
